summary: This standards-track memo defines MIB objects for managing Fibre Channel, a technology commonly used in storage networks. Network management tools can use them with SNMP to see information about Fibre Channel devices and links.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines standard SNMP data for managing Fibre Channel equipment. It lets management systems examine Fibre Channel ports, switches, links and traffic statistics in a consistent way.

questions: what is the fibre channel mib
how to monitor fibre channel with snmp
what is a world wide name
subtitle: A standard SNMP MIB for monitoring Fibre Channel instances, ports, switches, statistics and links.

tldr.problem: Fibre Channel devices need management data that fits the Internet-standard SNMP framework and its existing interface tables.
tldr.mechanism: FC-MGMT-MIB defines eleven groups of Fibre Channel objects and specifies how each port appears in the Interfaces Group MIB, including ifType 56.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4044 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 2837. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

today: RFC 4044 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2005. It obsoletes RFC 2837; the unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Fibre Channel Objects and Addresses
sections.content:
Fibre Channel is a bidirectional serial channel for transporting protocols such as SCSI and IP. Its ports connect directly, through a switch fabric, or through an arbitrated loop. Port roles include N_Ports, NL_Ports, F_Ports, FL_Ports, E_Ports and B_Ports.

Fibre Channel components commonly have World Wide Names (WWNs), which are expected to persist across agent and unit resets. Frames also carry 24-bit address identifiers for source and destination ports. A switch assigns these identifiers dynamically when a fabric is used.
sections.plainLanguage: Fibre Channel connects storage and other systems through ports and switches. A WWN identifies a component over time, while its 24-bit address can be assigned dynamically by a switch.

sections.title: The Eleven Management Groups
sections.content:
The FC-MGMT-MIB module organizes Fibre Channel-specific management information into eleven object groups. They describe managed instances, switches, ports, general and class-specific port statistics, lower-capacity counters, port errors, switch port settings, attached-port logins and links.

A management instance is a separable instance of Fibre Channel functionality. Implementations choose how to group that functionality. Tables use fcmInstanceIndex to distinguish multiple instances in one SNMP context.

Some traffic counters use Counter64 because they may increase rapidly. The fcmPortLcStatsGroup provides Counter32 versions for older SNMP systems that do not support Counter64.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIB separates information into eleven groups, including port details, traffic totals, errors and links. Each managed instance has an index so several instances can be distinguished.

sections.title: Using Standard Interface and Device MIBs
sections.content:
Each Fibre Channel port should have a row in the Interfaces Group MIB's ifTable. FC-MGMT-MIB supplies Fibre Channel-specific details and indexes its port tables by that row's ifIndex. It assigns Fibre Channel interfaces ifType 56.

The RFC also defines how generic interface counters and attributes apply. Octet counters count frame contents between the Start-of-Frame and End-of-Frame delimiters, excluding those delimiters. The Entity MIB and Host Resources MIB can provide optional links to the physical and software components associated with a management instance.

The module is named FC-MGMT-MIB and is registered as fcMgmtMIB under transmission 56. Fibre Channel objects complement the generic MIBs rather than replacing them.
sections.plainLanguage: Each Fibre Channel port appears in the standard interface table, with ifType 56. This MIB adds Fibre Channel details while leaving general device and interface information to other MIBs.

sections.title: Values, Ranges and Required Groups
sections.content:
The module defines standard types for Fibre Channel names, addresses, domain identifiers, credits, data field sizes, service classes and device functions. For example, a domain identifier ranges from 0 to 239, a buffer-to-buffer credit from 0 to 32767, and a data field size from 128 to 2112.

Implementations must support the instance-basic, port-basic and port-errors groups. Switch-specific groups are mandatory only for instances that manage Fibre Channel switches. The link-basic group is optional, and write access is not required for objects with read-write access in the module.

IANA assigned transmission 56 for the module and established a Fibre Channel port-type registry. Values up to 9,999 are for standardized types; 10,000 to 99,999 are for private use; larger values are reserved.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIB defines ranges and types so that management values have consistent meanings. Every implementation needs the basic instance, port and error groups, while switch and link groups depend on the equipment.

sections.title: Security and Earlier MIBs
sections.content:
Some read-write objects can change a port's type or speed, or a switch's domain identifier. Unauthorized changes can affect performance or cause denial of service. Readable link objects reveal network topology, so the RFC says access to GET and NOTIFY operations should also be controlled.

The RFC states that SNMP versions before SNMPv3 do not provide adequate security. It recommends SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy, and does not recommend deploying earlier versions. Operators remain responsible for configuring legitimate access.

RFC 4044 replaces RFC 2837 and the Fibre Channel Management Integration MIB. It removes generic objects that belong in other MIBs and clarifies how Fibre Channel interfaces use the standard interface table.
sections.plainLanguage: Management access can change network settings and reveal topology. The RFC recommends SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy, plus access controls for users and systems.

items.label: obsolete
items.desc: This value must not be reassigned.

items.label: NL_Port
items.desc: Node port on an arbitrated loop.

items.label: FL_Port
items.desc: Fabric port serving an arbitrated loop.

items.label: E_Port
items.desc: Port connecting to another switch port.

items.label: B_Port
items.desc: Connects a bridge device with an E_Port.

items.label: G_Port, GL_Port, F/NL_Port
items.desc: Types defined by Fibre Channel standards.
